mission_2.prediction: I predict BFS will finish sooner than DFS on the constrained map. In Mission 1, BFS found a 24.5 m route, while DFS found a much longer 104.0 m route. Although DFS expanded fewer nodes, that measures planning work rather than robot travel time. With the same controller and maximum speed, BFSs shorter route should generally require less travel time. Turns, obstacle clearance and tracking behavior could still affect the outcome, and DFS might reach the execution time limit.
mission_2.performance:
On the constrained map, BFS succeeded with elapsed_s = 90.700 and distance_m = 23.946. DFS returned controller_failed with elapsed_s = 30.988 and distance_m = 6.944. My prediction favored BFS because its planned route was 24.5 m, compared with DFSs 104.0 m route.

The result supports BFS as the better choice for completing this delivery, but it does not directly confirm which planner would finish sooner if both succeeded. DFSs shorter recorded time represents an early failure, not faster arrival. I retained the final checkpoint of the constrained DFS attempt as a stopped or failed approach. At that point, the recorded journey had ended approximately 8.252 m from the goal after travelling only 6.944 m. BFS completed its route instead. The controller reported error 104, but these results alone do not establish the exact cause of the failure.
mission_2.choice:
I would choose Nav2 Smac 2D for further delivery testing. It succeeded on the open map in 35.0 simulation seconds and on the constrained map in 73.5 seconds. BFS also succeeded on both maps, but took 46.7 seconds on the open map and 90.7 seconds on the constrained map.

Nav2 travelled approximately 10.046 m on the open map and 20.623 m on the constrained map, compared with BFSs 13.164 m and 23.946 m. Nav2 completed both deliveries with less travel and shorter execution time. Its mean tracking error was slightly higher than the BFSs, so it was not better on every measure.

The advantage that matters most for my choice is successful delivery with shorter execution time on both maps. Nav2 uses cost aware planning and smoothing, so it is a different system baseline from the four connected BFS implementation. There was only one recorded trial per planner on each map, so these results dont show reliable success rates.
